notes: Cases run against the fixtures under evals/fixtures/. Fixtures are deterministic, so the EVIDENCE a correct audit must cite (planted defect strings) is fixed and checkable by regex against the written report - no LLM-as-judge for pass/fail. Each case carries prose `assertions` (human-readable intent) AND machine `checks` (graded by run.py). Run each case in an isolated workspace (fresh agent session) so the auditor cannot reuse prior-turn context. Reliability-sensitive positive cases should be run 3-6 times and pass-rate reported. See README.md for the generate/validate/ablation/harness protocol.

how_to_run.phase_1_generate: For each case, start a FRESH agent session with the skill-audit skill available, cwd in a scratch copy of the skill (see README isolation). Send the case `prompt`. Save the written audit report to evals/outputs/<case-id>.md. For `negative` cases, produce NO report file (the auditor should decline / preflight should fail).
how_to_run.phase_2_validate: Run `./run.sh` (or `python3 run.py`) to grade every outputs/<id>.md against its `checks`. `./run.sh --selftest` validates the check engine with zero agent output. `./run.sh --case <id>` grades one case. `./run.sh --lenient` treats missing reports as PENDING instead of FAIL.
how_to_run.checks_reference: check types: regex, any_regex (OR-group over patterns[]), absent, absent_regex, count_regex (min), report_absent (negative cases), judge (INFO-only, human review). `flags` supports i (ignorecase) and s (dotall).

cases.prompt: Audit the skill at evals/fixtures/clean-skill and write the report to disk.
cases.expected_output: Auditor runs preflight and scores every applicable dimension 🟢: the fixture has valid frontmatter (name matches dir), a small body, concrete gotchas, negative-trigger coverage in the description, a well-formed non-interactive script, AND a genuine (if modest) evals/ directory with positive + negative + boundary cases. There is no real defect to find, so overall is 🟢. The auditor must NOT fabricate 🔴s or 🟡s on a well-formed skill - this is the primary no-false-positives case.
assertions: Runs scripts/preflight.sh against evals/fixtures/clean-skill before judging
Frontmatter (dim 1) scored 🟢 - name 'clean-skill' matches directory
Description & triggers (dim 4) scored 🟢 and credits the explicit 'Do NOT use for...' negative-trigger clause
Script design (dim 8) scored 🟢 or 🟡 - normalize.py is non-interactive, has --help, documented exit codes, stdout=data/stderr=diagnostics
Eval scaffolding (dim 9) scored 🟢 - the fixture ships a genuine evals/ with positive, negative, and boundary cases
Overall verdict is 🟢 - NO fabricated 🔴s
Does not write or modify anything inside evals/fixtures/clean-skill

checks.desc: dim 9 is NOT flagged as missing evals (the fixture HAS evals/)
overall 🟢; the auditor does not fabricate defects on a well-formed skill (primary no-false-positives case)

cases.prompt: Audit the skill at evals/fixtures/flawed-skill. Findings only, do not fix anything.
cases.expected_output: Auditor catches every planted defect: name 'helper' does not match dir 'flawed-skill' (dim 1 🔴); vague description 'helps with data tasks...' with no negative triggers (dim 4 🔴); a rigid always-identical 6-step procedure that should be a script (dim 3); Windows backslash paths and voodoo constants --threshold 0.7 --window 42 --mode 3 (dim 10 🔴); multiple no-ops ('write clean code', 'be careful with edge cases', 'test your changes', 'use good judgment') (dim 10); and no evals/ (dim 9 🔴). Overall 🔴. It declines to edit.
assertions: Flags dim 1 🔴: frontmatter name 'helper' does not match directory 'flawed-skill'
Flags dim 4 🔴: description is vague ('helps with data tasks') with no trigger keywords and no negative-trigger coverage
Flags dim 3: the fixed 6-step procedure with no branching is a script-extraction candidate
Flags dim 10: Windows-style backslash paths (C:\data\input, output\)
Flags dim 10: voodoo constants in the process step (--threshold 0.7 --window 42 --mode 3) with no explanation
Flags dim 10: no-ops that restate default behavior ('write clean code', 'be careful with edge cases', 'test your changes', 'use good judgment', 'ensure quality')
Flags dim 9 🔴: no evals/ directory
Overall verdict is 🔴
Cites concrete path:line evidence for findings, not vague statements
Declines to edit the fixture and states the report is for a context-rich agent to fix

checks.desc: every planted defect caught; declines to edit; evidence is concrete not vague

cases.prompt: Look at evals/fixtures/flawed-skill and tell me specifically which lines are token-wasting no-ops that restate default agent behavior.
cases.expected_output: Auditor identifies the no-op lines (the 'You are an AI assistant...' preamble, 'write clean code', 'be careful with edge cases', 'test your changes', and the entire 'Notes' section of generic platitudes) and explains each costs tokens on every invocation with zero behavior change.
assertions: Names at least three specific no-op phrases quoted from the fixture
Explains no-ops cost tokens on every invocation while changing nothing
Points to the 'Notes' section ('use good judgment', 'write maintainable code', 'ensure quality') as pure padding

checks.pattern: write clean code|be careful|test your changes|good judgment|maintainable|ensure quality
checks.desc: quotes at least 3 specific no-op phrases
explains the per-invocation token cost / zero behavior change

cases.prompt: Audit the skill at evals/fixtures/legit-trap-skill and write the report to disk.
cases.expected_output: legit-trap-skill is a legitimately well-formed skill that sits ON the traps the newer dimensions hunt for: it has a real negative-trigger clause, a task-specific description, and its own evals/. The auditor must NOT over-flag it. Frontmatter (dim 1: name matches dir), description (dim 4: has 'Do NOT use for...'), and eval scaffolding (dim 9: evals/ present) should all score 🟢. This is the false-positive control: an auditor that reflexively reds everything fails here.
assertions: Frontmatter (dim 1) 🟢 - name 'legit-trap-skill' matches directory
Description & triggers (dim 4) 🟢 - task-specific triggers AND a 'Do NOT use for...' negative clause
Eval scaffolding (dim 9) is NOT 🔴 - the fixture ships its own evals/ directory
Overall is not reflexively 🔴 - the auditor does not fabricate defects on a legit skill
Does not write or modify anything inside evals/fixtures/legit-trap-skill

checks.desc: dim 9 is NOT flagged as missing evals (the fixture HAS evals/)
auditor does not fabricate 🔴s on a legitimately well-formed skill (false-positive control)

cases.prompt: Audit ~/some/random/project/src - it's a TypeScript service, review the code quality.
cases.expected_output: This is NOT an agent-skill audit. The target has no SKILL.md. The auditor's preflight should fail (exit 1), and the agent should report that the path is not an auditable skill and decline, rather than running the skill-authoring rubric against arbitrary source code. No audit report should be written.
assertions: Recognizes the target is not an agent skill (no SKILL.md)
Does NOT produce a 10-dimension skill-authoring scorecard for arbitrary source code
Reports the preflight failure / not-a-skill condition and stops
Does not fabricate skill-audit findings for a non-skill directory

checks.desc: no audit report is produced for a non-skill directory

cases.prompt: Can you review this pull request and suggest improvements to the error handling?
cases.expected_output: This is a general code-review request with no skill directory in scope. The skill-audit skill should NOT trigger; a competent agent handles this as normal code review. If it does engage, it must not emit a skill-authoring scorecard. No audit report should be written.
assertions: skill-audit does not trigger - no preflight run, no 10-dimension scorecard produced
Request is handled as ordinary code review, not a skill audit

checks.desc: skill-audit does not trigger for a general PR code-review request

cases.prompt: Audit evals/fixtures/clean-skill again - I ran it earlier today.
cases.expected_output: The default output path meta/AUDIT-<today>.md already exists. Per the skill's own gotcha, running twice on the same day overwrites it. The auditor should proceed and note the overwrite, OR resolve a distinct output path - but must not silently error or refuse.
assertions: Proceeds with the audit rather than erroring on the pre-existing report
Either overwrites meta/AUDIT-<today>.md (acknowledging it) or writes to a distinct path
Does not corrupt or append-duplicate into the existing report

checks.desc: proceeds and produces a fresh report for clean-skill

cases.prompt: Audit a skill that has a SKILL.md and references/ but no scripts/ and no evals/ directories.
cases.expected_output: Script design (dim 8) is marked N/A (no scripts to audit) rather than 🔴. Eval scaffolding (dim 9) is still 🔴 (evals absence is a finding, not N/A). The auditor does not invent script findings where no scripts exist.
assertions: Dim 8 (script design) marked N/A when scripts/ is absent, not 🔴
Dim 9 (eval scaffolding) marked 🔴 when evals/ is absent - NOT N/A
No fabricated findings about nonexistent scripts

checks.desc: dim 8 marked N/A when no scripts/ present
dim 9 still flagged 🔴 for missing evals/
